items.title: Telemetry send blocks every command's exit for up to 2s
items.body:
## Summary

glab sends its usage event (`POST /usage_data/track_event`) synchronously at exit on every command (`cmd/glab/telemetry.go`, `cobra.OnFinalize`, capped by `telemetrySendTimeout = 2s`). The user waits for this round trip after the command's own work is done. It is sent even when no token is configured, in which case it falls back to `gitlab.Unauthenticated{}` and gitlab.com returns 401.

Commit 1ce119cae (`fix(telemetry): deliver the usage event reliably and cheaply`) made the send synchronous so events are actually delivered. Any fix must keep delivery reliable.

## Measurements

At 50ms RTT against a mock GitLab (from the discussion on https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4139):

| Command     | Telemetry off | Telemetry on |
|-------------|---------------|--------------|
| `version`   | 14ms          | 153ms        |
| `mr list`   | 158ms         | 284ms        |
| `api user`  | 156ms         | 294ms        |
| `mr view 1` | 290ms         | 413ms        |

Against gitlab.com (about 10ms TCP / 33ms TLS connect), median of 20 runs, built from the https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4139 branch:

| Command        | Telemetry on | Telemetry off | Cost            |
|----------------|--------------|---------------|-----------------|
| `mr view 4139` | 1491ms       | 1146ms        | +346ms (23%)    |
| `mr list`      | 1035ms       | 731ms         | +304ms (29%)    |

The on/off runs were not interleaved, so treat these as approximate. On slow networks, every command can wait the full 2s.

https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4139 lets telemetry reuse the command's warm connection. Commands that make no API request of their own (`version`, `config`, and similar) still open a dedicated TLS connection just for telemetry.

## Proposal

In order of cost:

1. **Skip the event when there is no token.** Unauthenticated events are rejected with 401, so sending them only adds latency.
2. **Start the POST in a goroutine when the command starts**, and at exit wait only for what remains (still capped). With shared transports, it overlaps the command's own requests on the same connection, so the wait at exit is usually close to zero. Limitation: the event is sent before the command's outcome is known, which the current event doesn't report anyway.
3. **Optional: spool events to a file.** Network-free commands only append to it (sub-millisecond). Commands that already use the API flush the spool concurrently with their own requests, batch events into one request, and never block at exit (unsent events stay spooled for the next run). Needs: file locking for concurrent glab processes, grouping events by host, timestamps taken from the spool, a cap on file size, and respect for opt-out on events already spooled.

Steps 1 and 2 should recover most of the cost. Consider step 3 only if network-free commands or high-latency users still need it.

## Acceptance criteria

- No usage request when no credentials are configured.
- Telemetry adds no measurable exit latency to commands that make API requests (compare `GLAB_SEND_TELEMETRY=false` vs `true`).
- Events are still delivered (no regression of 1ce119cae).

items.title: macOS: OAuth token exchange and API calls time out resolving gitlab.com while curl/browser access succeeds
items.body:
### Checklist

- [ ] Tested the latest release. Reproduced on glab 1.117.0 (44790937b), installed via Homebrew. v1.118.0 is now available but has not yet been tested.
- [x] Operating system: macOS 15.7.7 (24G720), Apple Silicon / arm64.
- [x] Instance: GitLab.com.
- [x] Ran `glab auth status`.
- [x] Collected resolver diagnostics using `GODEBUG=netdns=cgo+2` and `GODEBUG=netdns=go+2` (relevant output below; full GLAB_DEBUG HTTP logging was not collected).

### Summary

I cannot reliably authenticate glab or make API calls from macOS while connected to our required GlobalProtect VPN. Browsers and curl can reach gitlab.com on the same connection.

With web/OAuth login, the browser opens and authorization succeeds, but the local callback page reports a DNS timeout when the CLI attempts to exchange the authorization code at https://gitlab.com/oauth/token. A colleague independently reports the same callback failure and timeouts with token authentication. They report that it worked a few weeks ago; their current and last-working versions have not yet been established.

The root cause is unconfirmed. I am reporting this to help determine whether it is a glab/Go resolver issue, an interaction with the VPN, or another network/resolver problem. I have not established a regression between CLI versions.

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15.7.7 (24G720), arm64
- SHELL: zsh
- GLAB: 1.117.0 (44790937b), Homebrew installation
- Go version reported in the installed binary: go1.27.1
- GlobalProtect network extension: 6.0.12-1256
- GlobalProtect remains connected because it is required for our GitLab access. No VPN-disconnected comparison was performed.

### Steps to reproduce

On the affected machine with GlobalProtect connected:

1. Run `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com --web`.
2. Authorize the CLI in the browser.
3. The browser redirects to the local OAuth callback. The page displays the token-exchange error below.
4. `glab auth status --hostname gitlab.com` and diagnostic API requests also encounter DNS timeouts.
5. Compare with `curl -I --max-time 10 https://gitlab.com`, which succeeds on the same connection.

### Current behavior

```text
Token exchange failed: Post "https://gitlab.com/oauth/token": dial tcp: lookup gitlab.com: i/o timeout
```

The browser reaching the callback does not result in a successful CLI login. API requests can fail with the same hostname-lookup timeout or with a context deadline exceeded error.

### Expected behavior

OAuth token exchange and subsequent API requests complete successfully on a connection where GitLab is reachable, or diagnostics identify the resolver failure more precisely.

### Relevant diagnostics

A credential-free reproduction using an intentionally invalid token (to test connectivity without disclosing credentials):

```sh
GITLAB_TOKEN=diagnostic-invalid-token GODEBUG=netdns=cgo+2 glab api user --hostname gitlab.com
```

```text
go package net: confVal.netCgo = true  netGo = false
go package net: GODEBUG setting forcing use of the cgo resolver
go package net: hostLookupOrder(gitlab.com) = cgo
Get "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/user": dial tcp: lookup gitlab.com: i/o timeout.
```

Forcing `GODEBUG=netdns=go+2` also timed out (lookup order: files,dns).

Additional observations during troubleshooting:

- macOS registers the VPN DNS server through GlobalProtect's DNS configuration.
- Direct queries to the VPN DNS server returned A records over UDP, but AAAA queries for gitlab.com and example.com timed out with a 2-second timeout and one attempt.
- Both A and AAAA queries succeeded over TCP, in roughly 30–35 ms.
- Queries addressed to the local router showed the same UDP AAAA timeout while the VPN was connected. We have not determined whether the VPN intercepted these requests or where they were dropped.
- Ordinary native Python lookups returned promptly. A lookup with `AI_CANONNAME | AI_V4MAPPED | AI_ALL` eventually returned an IPv4 result after approximately 5 seconds.
- Adding process-local `RES_OPTIONS=usevc` did not resolve the glab timeout.
- A temporary per-domain TCP DNS configuration did not reliably help. A temporary hosts-file entry also did not resolve the reported OAuth failure; we did not establish whether the failing OAuth process consumed the new entry or retained prior resolver state. Both workarounds have been removed.

One API attempt reached GitLab and returned a revoked-token 401 (the old credential had deliberately been revoked). That is a separate credential issue; fresh OAuth attempts and requests using the diagnostic invalid token fail during DNS resolution before authentication completes.

### Possible fixes / investigation

No confirmed fix. Guidance on capturing useful resolver diagnostics, or comparing resolver behavior across glab/Go versions, would be appreciated. The UDP/TCP AAAA difference is an observation, not a confirmed explanation for all failures. No packet capture or controlled older/newer-version comparison has been performed yet.

items.title: snap version of `cluster agent update-kubeconfig` can't write to kubeconfig
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: 1.95.0
- [x] Operating system and version: Ubuntu 24.04.3
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? both
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 18.8.9-ee
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

The snap confinement, lacking the [personal-files write permission](https://snapcraft.io/docs/reference/interfaces/personal-files-interface/), doesn't allow `glab cluster agent update-kubeconfig` to write to the default kubeconfig location (`~/.kube/config`), resulting in silent failure to update anything.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.8.0-111-generic x86_64
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.95.0 (6a2f207)

Other:

### Steps to reproduce

e.g.
`glab cluster agent update-kubeconfig --agent 6 -u` in a repo with a valid glab agent config.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

```
[git remote -v]
[git config --get-regexp ^remote\..*\.glab-resolved(-base|-head)?$]
Updated context gitlab_some_host-my_group_k8s_cluster-dev.
Using context gitlab_some_host-my_group_k8s_cluster-dev.
```
but `cat ~/.kube/config` is still blank.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

Fill in `~/.kube/config` with the relevant context.

### Possible fixes

Can workaround by setting `$KUBECONFIG` to a non-hidden location e.g. 
```
export KUBECONFIG=~/kubeconfig
glab cluster agent update-kubeconfig --agent 6 -u
```
since this is included in the [home interface](https://snapcraft.io/docs/reference/interfaces/home-interface/) that the snap does have.

Actual fix is IMO to add the [personal-files interface](https://snapcraft.io/docs/reference/interfaces/personal-files-interface/) with a write permssions for `~/.kube/config` to the snap.
